chunks: Al-Husayn ibn Sa'id from al-Qasim ibn Muhammad and Fadalah from Aban from Ubayd ibn Zur'arah said:

I said to Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him): A man pledged two bracelets, and one of them was lost. He said: 'He reverts to what remains.' And he said regarding a man who pledged a house to him, which was burned or collapsed: 'His wealth is in the dust of the earth.'
ai.seo_question: What happens to the debt if the pledged item is lost or destroyed?
ai.summary: Recorded in Shaykh al-Tusi’s *Tahdhib al-Ahkam* from the chain of Ubayd ibn Zurara, this hadith clarifies the distribution of risk in pledge (*rahn*) contracts under Imam al-Sadiq (AS). It establishes that if one of two pledged items is lost, the debtor remains liable for the value of the remaining item, whereas if the pledged property is entirely destroyed or collapses, the creditor bears the loss, as the debtor’s obligation is extinguished. This ruling highlights the Shia jurisprudential principle that the risk of loss in a pledge generally falls on the creditor unless otherwise specified, ensuring fairness in commercial transactions.
